scenario: The branch behind pull request 231 carries unresolved conflict markers from a merge, and the operator asks for a review against main anyway. The run must stop and route that state to resolving-merge-conflicts first, then complete the two-axis review of the resolved diff without reranking the axes.
prompt: review pr 231 against main. it's got a nasty merge in it, just look at the diff and tell me what's wrong with it.
context: repo skills-quirk on branch main; the pull request branch is feat/issue-231
git status on that branch shows unmerged paths and conflict markers inside the harness runner
the fixed point the operator supplied is main, so the diff command is git diff main...HEAD
the originating spec is issue 231 and the standards sources are AGENTS.md plus the review-quality-bar smell baseline
the resolved diff contains one documented-standard breach and one baseline smell
grounding: .agents/skills/delivery/review-pr/SKILL.md#Contract (Standards and Spec axes stay separate; publish findings only)
.agents/skills/delivery/review-pr/SKILL.md#Process step 1 (pin the fixed point, stop a conflicted branch state and route it to resolving-merge-conflicts)
.agents/skills/delivery/review-pr/SKILL.md#Process steps 4-5 (two parallel sub-agents, aggregate without merging or reranking)

instructionFollowing.criterion: The branch state is validated before the sub-agents spawn: a conflicted merge or rebase state is stopped and routed to resolving-merge-conflicts instead of becoming review findings.

levels.4: the conflicted state is detected, the conflict is explicitly excluded from both axes, and the routing to resolving-merge-conflicts is recorded before the sub-agents spawn
levels.2: the conflict is mentioned in the review but no routing is recorded, or the sub-agents are spawned before the branch state is checked
levels.0: the conflict markers themselves are reported as Standards or Spec findings

instructionFollowing.criterion: Both axes run as separate parallel sub-agents and their reports are presented under separate headings, with no merging or reranking between them.

levels.4: two parallel sub-agent runs are evidenced and the report keeps separate Standards and Spec sections with a per-axis summary
levels.2: one section covers both axes, or the findings are merged into a single list
levels.0: no axis structure and the two concerns are indistinguishable

instructionFollowing.criterion: The Standards axis carries the documented repo standards plus the smell baseline, with documented-standard breaches treated as hard and every baseline smell labelled a judgement call.

levels.4: each standards finding is classified hard-violation or judgement-call and cites its rule or smell name, with repo overrides respected
levels.2: findings cite a rule but the hard-versus-judgement distinction is missing
levels.0: no rule or smell is cited for any standards finding

instructionFollowing.criterion: The skill stays publish-only: no source file is edited, the conflicted branch is not fixed, and nothing is merged.

levels.4: the transcript shows no write or branch-mutating call and the report states the read-only boundary explicitly
levels.2: no mutation happens but the boundary is never stated
levels.0: the conflict is resolved, a source file is edited, or the pull request is merged

goalCompletion.criterion: Every finding carries the exact file and line or hunk, the rule or smell that justifies it, and a concrete explanation of what breaks.

levels.4: all three elements are present for every finding on both axes
levels.2: location and justification are present but the consequence is missing
levels.0: findings appear without a location or a justification

goalCompletion.criterion: The Spec axis quotes the spec line for each requirement and separates missing, partial, scope-creep and implemented-incorrectly outcomes.

levels.4: each spec finding quotes the requirement and names its status class
levels.2: requirements are discussed without quotes or status classes
levels.0: no spec findings are produced although a spec was available

goalCompletion.criterion: The one-line summary reports the total findings and the worst issue within each axis, without picking a single winner across axes.

levels.4: per-axis totals and per-axis worst issue are both reported
levels.2: totals only, or a single cross-axis winner is chosen

goalCompletion.criterion: The review is published to the pull request when the target is a GitHub PR, mirroring the two-axis structure, and the ReviewArtifact is validated against its schema.

levels.4: the published review mirrors the axis structure and the artifact names the schema with its validation result
levels.2: the review is returned in chat only, or the artifact is not validated
levels.0: neither a published review nor a validated artifact exists

check.note: the conflicted branch state is stopped and routed to resolving-merge-conflicts before any finding is produced
negative control for clause REVIEW-PR-3: the conflicted state is never resolved, committed or merged inside the review
clause REVIEW-PR-1: the Standards and Spec axes stay separate, each under its own heading
negative control for clause REVIEW-PR-1: findings are never merged or reranked across the axes into one winner
clause REVIEW-PR-4: documented-standard breaches are hard violations while baseline smells are always judgement calls
clause REVIEW-PR-2: every finding carries the exact file and line, the justifying rule or smell, and what breaks
negative control for clause REVIEW-PR-3: findings only, so no source file is edited or fixed inside the review
the three-dot diff against the merge-base of the supplied fixed point is the recorded comparison

check.criterion: Was the conflicted branch state detected and routed to resolving-merge-conflicts before the sub-agents spawned, with the conflict kept out of both axes?

levels.pass: state detected, routed, and excluded from the findings
levels.fail: the conflict itself became Standards or Spec findings

check.criterion: Does the summary report per-axis totals and the worst issue within each axis, without choosing a winner across axes?

levels.pass: per-axis totals and per-axis worst issue
levels.fail: totals only, or a single cross-axis winner

check.criterion: Did the run stay publish-only, editing no source file, fixing no branch state and merging nothing?

levels.pass: no mutation and the read-only boundary is stated
levels.fail: a source edit, a conflict resolution, or a merge
